subject: Re: Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr) — heritage research and a Welsh museum project in Patagonia
source: Original email in the family's Gmail (read-only export); contact details redacted.
text:
Dear Mr Buckler,

Thanks for your email of 20th September 2026.

I note that our Clerk, Paul Egan, has already directed you to all the 
information we have on the matter as indicated in paragraph 6 of your 
email.

We have nothing more to add.

Best regards

Dr M C Misra,

Chair Llandough Community Council

On 2026-09-20 07:29, Sion Buckler wrote:

> Councillor Misra & Co,
> 
> My family, the Williams and later Buckler family, lived at Great House 
> Farm (Tŷ Mawr) beside St Dochdwy's for almost 4 consecutive centuries 
> until 1988, when our 800 year old 10 bed manorial home was subject to 
> an SAS style siege and demolished. I was born there. The site is now 
> Church View Close.
> 
> That whole incident appears to stem from a 1955 possession order for a 
> parcel of land east of the parcel we held freehold of. The order 
> contained ambiguity that was later misinterprited to make our occupancy 
> of our parcel appear permissive, following our paper title copy being 
> stolen. A 1962 possession order for our parcel was created based on 
> that but not enforced on my disabled, widow grandmother. Who just had a 
> leg amputated in 1955. Instead the interest in the 1962 order was 
> conveyed from Western Ground Rents to BP in 1969. BP altered the 
> ordinance survey, shifting the descriptor from their parcel onto my 
> nans. And appending "farm' to it. They again made her occupancy appear 
> pernissive in 1974 with their famous licence letters. Then conveyed 
> interest in that, again, to their own sister company in 1975. Not 
> withstanding the possession of the 1962 order was quashed in 1974. Also 
> in 1974 my nans ownership claim was not legally exstiguished and 
> instead the court ajourned. In 1983 BP then quietly registered our land 
> in their names at the land registry, failing to disclose my nans 
> ownership claim, she also died in the 2 weeks she will have had to 
> challenge them. She had not been known to not challenge them in decades 
> of her campaigning. Land registry also didn't notify her/ us. BP then 
> merged our parcel into theirs, as my nan fought for her life and died. 
> The land registry wrote to the MP this week claiming not find anything 
> wrong with the role they played in 1982/1983. .
> 
> In 1877 title became our families from Daniel Thomas & Son. But not 
> until 1928 when quarrying completed on the land. In 1916 Bute produced 
> an agrictural tenancy for our family featuring our occupied parcel and 
> a parcel to the east. The interest in this is what conveyed to Western 
> Ground Rents in 1938. And in 1939 they revised the agreement for the 
> parcel east of ours. And excluded ours parcel from any tenancy due to 
> the 1928 event and my great grandads registration of the freehold.
> 
> The 1877 - 1928 agreement and title deed was stolen from our home 
> according to my late nans statement in these proceedings.
> 
> When WGR saught possession of their parcel to the east of ours in 1955, 
> they exercised moral hazard to introduce ambiguity into the order, 
> considering my nans vulnerable state (amputee, widow, pensioner, stolen 
> title deed), which could have and did get later misinterprited to make 
> my nans occupancy appear permissive. And Western Ground Rents the 
> owner. Thus fabricating a defective title with the 1962 possession 
> order for my nans parcel and through conveying that unenforced 
> possession order to BP in 1969. BPs permissive occupancy licence in 
> 1974 and 1975 conveyance repeated that process to make interest 
> transfer and a title chain emerge, with no root title.
> 
> Mr Paul Egan answered a request from me on 14 June this year. He 
> searched the Council's records, explained that the minute books from 
> 1982 onward were deposited with Glamorgan Archives in 2002, set out the 
> section 21 position correctly, and pointed me to the Council's own 
> pages on buildings of significance in the community. He also told me 
> something I had not known -- that before 1982 Llandough came under 
> Penarth Town Council -- which has opened a line of research I would 
> otherwise have missed. I had written to him in strong terms and he 
> replied with courtesy and care anyway. I understand he has since 
> retired after long service to the village. Please pass on my thanks if 
> you are able to. I am not asking the Council to revisit his answer; it 
> was a proper one.
> 
> I am assembling a complete documentary and photographic record of my 
> family's old manorial 10-bedroom birth and family home since 1667, at 
> the centre of that church you British built in the 1800s -- I am 
> interested in everything: planning, archaeology, land registration, 
> family papers, oral memory -- all into a single, centralised searchable 
> archive. So the actual full story can be retold. Warts and all.
> 
> Please bear with me for the rest of my email. I was traumatised by our 
> experience being dispossessed in the 80's. We've seen no justice. My 
> family died challenging any of the false narrative. And the remaining 
> alive won't speak up. The State have tried covering this up and 
> continue to do so for decades too. I'm the first to try to bring this 
> all to light.
> 
> My intent with all this is a Welsh heritage project I have underway in 
> Patagonia, Argentina, where a replica of my old farm is to be 
> constructed as a museum.
> 
> In Argentina they are different from you British currently occupying us 
> Welsh in Wales, in that they celebrate and don't supress or conceal our 
> Welsh heritage, culture, language, history. It is very refreshing for 
> me there, as an indigenous Briton who was brutally torn from my 
> ancestral birthland in 1988, in what can only be described as ethnic 
> cleansing. I am not even exaggerating; the particulars of the horrors 
> done to my family there make reconstructing the full chronology very 
> challenging. It's not new what Brit'ish do to indigenous people 
> globally, or the Welsh historically. But we were maybe the last to be 
> annexed, colonised and looted in such a systematic and brutal way.
> 
> It would be passable if we were sincerely squatters being evicted as 
> the press reported. Or even courts believed. But the land BP possessed 
> they had. We lost the parcel east of ours fair and square. They came to 
> occupy our neighbouring land and home too out of greed, to build Church 
> View Close. Using force, stealth/ secrecy and license. The destinction 
> would have been clear had BP not registered our land in their names and 
> merged ours into theirs, in such a clandestine way, in 1982/1983.
> 
> So much of my family's and people's history and heritage in Llandough 
> continues to be completely covered up in lieu of those 20 characterless 
> (Church View Close) concentration work-camp houses, without so much as 
> a park-bench plaque to commemorate any of the following:
> 
> - the 1,026 medieval burials
> - Marconi staying with us while inventing radio
> - Peerless Joe Driscoll fighting his first fight in our barn
> - the Roman villa
> - Christian monastery
> - 2,200-year-old Celtic roundhouse
> 
> the list goes on. The LiDAR scans etc.
> 
> I find it abhorrent that the Llandough website history page does not 
> mention any of this either. I know the British are proud of their No.1 
> invention: the concentration work camp -- but it is sad witnessing all 
> our towns and cities being turned into them. Not that I am on the 
> British Isles much, except occasionally as a sort of autochthonous 
> Django Unchained. Seeing all the voters being imported to keep the 
> kinds of governors, Princess of Darkness and demons the Bible warns us 
> about in power does not even sadden me anymore. I think crusades may 
> happen sooner as a result, and therein resides my hope for my small 
> pale island.
> 
> It was not always such a demonic realm for us natives, nor our 
> non-indigenous actual guests, friends and family in Llandough. My 
> family lived in the main manorial house in Llandough consecutively 
> since 1667 until the British's highly illegal, unlawful and 
> unconstitutional siege and theft of our stronghold in 1988. We still 
> appear to own the land under Church View Close. You British only 
> awarded yourselves possession of our Christian stronghold. Possession 
> being the weapon of choice of a demonic realm. When I was a soldier in 
> Cyprus I would enjoy watching the UN hand back stolen, occupied land to 
> the Greeks and Turks. I look forward to that occurring when Wales 
> literally, not figuratively, decolonises. Or Scotland renounces. Or 
> Ireland unites. I see the British State as more of a terrorist 
> organisation than the IRA, and I think it is the British State we need 
> to stop harbouring on our motherland.
> 
> In the interim of revolution, I hold some faith in coalitions. Namely 
> thanks to Councillor Chris Franks, my grandmother's old good friend of 
> decades, who at least acknowledged my email. And that a grave injustice 
> does appear to have occurred to my family and, as a matter of public 
> interest, others too. To be brutally honest I think my case shows signs 
> we are in a landmark bubble and a land-market crash is coming. This 
> racket of converting amputee, disabled widow pensioners' occupancy of 
> our lands from freehold to permissive (with ambiguity and 
> misinterpretation and fraud and concealment) possession orders and 
> conveyance, stealth/secrecy etc. -- was not a sustainable viable way of 
> annexing. You can fool some of the people some of the time. But not all 
> of the people all of the time.
> 
> But this is a request for co-operation with reconstructing history, not 
> a complaint. And history which has already been driven to lands many 
> thousands of miles away, so it can remain buried in the British's 
> wardrobe of skeletons as you so wish.
> 
> With 99% of British MPs refusing to sign EDM 2025 condemning 
> decapitating Christians, I think Argentina is an apt location for my 
> replica manorial house, notwithstanding Michael Jones who founded the 
> settlement in Patagonia had followers who even nicknamed the reason for 
> it as being the "decapitation committee" here on the British Isles (a 
> century after we acquired my birth home in Llandough, so some time in 
> the late 1700s).
> 
> In the interests of being straight with you: I had difficulty getting 
> replies from the Vale ward member, Councillor George Carroll, and 
> earlier this year I made a formal complaint to the Vale of Glamorgan 
> about that. Which I was surprised at after he got thrown out of a 
> council meeting for being against the City of Sanctuary scheme. My 
> motto is, if you are not on a government watchlist by now, you should 
> be ashamed of yourself.
> 
> I am already resigned to flying in and out of this small formerly pale 
> island, like it is another military tour of the Middle East. I actually 
> do not harbour much ill will; I am just sad it has gone to the dogs and 
> half expect a nuclear strike, flood or crusade.
> 
> My advice to my followers is not even to keep defending the 
> concentration work camps our hijacked towns and cities have been turned 
> into. Instead I encourage soldiers under my command to enjoy exile or 
> mass exodus. There is plenty in the British organisations' cells/camps 
> and networks' own rules which permits corps and exodusers. That way 
> everyone's happy.
> 
> The British State is not the first regime to go rogue. Terrorist 
> organisations (now the official government) like in Afghanistan also 
> have hostages and prisoners of war who are masochist submissives, like 
> British/UK citizens. And it is a situationship that suits both parties. 
> But not something I would want to get in the middle of or encourage 
> others to get in the middle of. I do not know why so many do.
> 
> I am persuaded to organise veterans to attend funerals of casualties of 
> the civil war our infiltrated, hijacked and traitor-filled regimes 
> waged on indigenous Britons, with its biological weapons, hybrid 
> warfare, ethnic cleansing and so forth. And we simply wear our uniforms 
> and salute the casualties. It is some remedy for the grieving families 
> who, even if speaking out from the decades of being terrorised into 
> silence, face decades of being stonewalled from justice from the State. 
> So I am all about the peaceful, legal and lawful paths forward -- as a 
> bona fide, certified, experienced military commander, leader and 
> warfare professional.
> 
> I have seen Councillor Carroll's recent social media posts standing in 
> front of the photograph of my old farm's only public photo that hangs 
> in the Merry Harrier pub. If it is in good faith and support I am glad. 
> Anything less I would not be surprised. Only disappointed. But I extend 
> the benefit of the doubt with my farm case, because it is a complex 
> case. Even in my profession as a seasoned cyber/electronic military 
> warfare professional I find it colossal to navigate.
> 
> What I would be grateful for from you who occupy and rule my land, in 
> place of your Pharisee predecessors, is a coalition with 
> counter-officers such as myself.
> 
> Does your occupying forces/council hold any records that were created 
> after 2002 and therefore not part of the 2002 deposit, concerning our 
> stolen, occupied Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr/Cedfin)/Church View Close 
> land?
> 
> And I should add: suspected, as I am still gathering evidence and 
> investigating. Albeit it all looks damning for the British and many 
> native traitors already, and I am only scratching the surface of what 
> happened in Llandough. My ancestral birthland would not be the first to 
> be looted by the British and I am doubtful it will be the last. Our 
> SAS-looted treasures are actually now all captive in British museums. 
> And our SAS-looted furniture, all from Cardiff Castle, are also held 
> hostage or in circulation too.
> 
> My focus and what I require of your Council, as but a humble 
> (registered to vote) constituent of the home we got in Dinas Powys and 
> have lived in since our land became illegally occupied by the British 
> in 1988 -- is the village green in front of St Dochdwy's -- including 
> registered village green VG 41, which your Council raised formally with 
> the Vale when the Great House Farm site came forward for planning in 
> 1989.
> 
> By constituent I do mean I am happy to play the role of a member of 
> society in a democracy. Albeit it is largely now pageantry and being 
> made a mockery of in my estimation. I see something very different 
> going on here, i.e. a terrorist/hostage situationship. And I do not 
> play the role of a hostage or prisoner of war well -- at all! Nor am I 
> a masochist submissive and much like kissing ring fingers or bending 
> knees. My 22 in Oath ended in 2024 (employed under the Vale of 
> Glamorgan Council too, by some freak coincidence). So I will thank you 
> in advance not to ask weird stuff of me. I am nice until it is time not 
> to be. And I believe we are all equal under law and God.
> 
> My family have endured enough force, stealth/secrecy and licence from 
> the British in the 80s to last us a lifetime. And having been behind a 
> machine gun in a helicopter in the Middle East, and trained on 
> explosives and weapons and cyber/electronic warfare capabilities for my 
> military career, which I left with full honours, I am well aware of how 
> the British regime operates and human-farms and projects its force. I 
> once had Britain's very own woke mind virus walking through my mind 
> with its muddy boots. I hope you all get better too.
> 
> Better your cell/network/camp just skip to bringing guns and trying to 
> force me at gunpoint if you demand anything of me that contrasts 
> co-operation or coalition. I have seen already a lot of local 
> authorities, even South Wales Police, opting for clandestine and 
> shadowy silence and violence, rather than just responding to public 
> FOIs. I think your regime's attempt to keep our Llandough farm story 
> from ever seeing the light of day is understandable. But I do find 
> people from time to time, even Iraqis in Iraq, even myself as a former 
> British soldier, wanting to choose the right side of history rather 
> than allegiance to a sinking rat ship.
> 
> Any record of works carried out on the green and the roadside verge by 
> the churchyard wall in the mid-1980s is all I am asking for. I hold 
> colour photographs of trees being removed, spoil carted away and new 
> kerbstones laid; vehicle registrations in them date the works to 
> between about 1983 and 1990, on more than one occasion. (See attached.) 
> Councillor Carroll's months of non-response to this specific request to 
> find this information out was not going to stop me finding all this 
> out. Asking for transparency and co-operation is mainly a courtesy and 
> formality, seeing as I am a seasoned military cyber/electronic warfare 
> professional. Going on 30 years now in fact.
> 
> My great-grandfather planted a tree on that green to mark my family's 
> claim to that land, and my family believe that tree was lost in the 
> work of making that green, i.e. possible further destruction of 
> evidence, possibly nothing. I should be clear that the green does not 
> even appear to fall inside the boundary of land we have the interest 
> in, in our ancestral town you currently occupy, so this is a question 
> about the village's history as much as ours.
> 
> Any photographs, postcards or images of the farm, the barn, the green 
> or the church surroundings that the Council holds or knows of. Please 
> disclose. I have vacuumed most of Leckwith Archives already.
> 
> Any guidance on where the pre-1982 community records now sit, given 
> that Llandough fell within Penarth Town Council before then, and 
> whether the Council holds anything that came across at the 1982 
> reorganisation, I would like you to please disclose.
> 
> The names of any former members, former clerks or long-standing 
> residents who might be willing to talk to me about the village between 
> the 1950s and the 1990s. I would approach anyone you suggest 
> courteously and would not press a refusal. Please disclose.
> 
> I am content for this email to be tabled at a meeting and minuted if 
> the Council wishes.
> I am also happy to give a short talk to the Council or the community, 
> without charge, on what the records have revealed about Llandough's 
> past -- the Roman villa, the early medieval cemetery beneath Church 
> View Close, the monastic history, and the farm itself.
> 
> A good deal of what I have found belongs to the village as much as my 
> family. Llandough just appears more committed to its current trajectory 
> of becoming even more of a concentration work camp, having already 
> rejected much of this history and heritage and native people, in lieu 
> of whatever it is you have underway there. I am not going to burn 
> Llandough down to feel its warmth. I know demonic realms are inherently 
> ice cold. To give an example of what I speak of, I found the Llandough 
> Facebook page to contain only photos of exotic takeaway foods. Sad 
> considering its rich history and heritage.
> 
> I am not about leading my men to spill their lifeblood on Home Office 
> Mahmoods and other British blades, over any of this demographic 
> replacement and ethnic cleansing. I am just trying to salvage, 
> reconstruct a part of my family's and Welsh history and heritage while 
> people still have heads on their shoulders here, to be able to 
> co-operate in this matter. Even without civil unrest, alleged 
> fiduciaries have not kept proper records of this case. Mine may be more 
> complete than the British Government's and EU's at this point. And even 
> the Internet's, considering the heirlooms I have inherited.
> 
> Regards,
> 
> Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
> Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member
> 
> P.S. Vehicle registrations visible in them (including A305 MKG, which 
> cannot predate August 1983, and plant registered MTX 936X and MTX 930X) 
> place the works in the mid-1980s, between 1983 and 1990, and not during 
> the later residential development.
